summary: Re-judge the weapon pair that was void in the first gauntlet (empty frame from a capture-harness fault)
logs: weapon pair re-judged: 0/3 wins, 0/3 mistaken for the real game

panel.why: A's rifle has individually beveled rail teeth catching orange rim light off the explosion, a numbered optic turret, worn edge highlights along the receiver, and a tumbling brass case with a readable primer face and extractor groove, while B is a flat-shaded slab with no hands, no trigger group, no magazine, no contact shadows anywhere in the scene, and a smeared foreground ground that stays sharp on distant buildings.
panel.weaponCraft: Proportions read as an unresolved kitbash: a bare capsule barrel with a flat open cap, a wood-grain plank abutting nothing structural, and a receiver slab carrying no trigger, trigger guard, magazine, pistol grip, or hands, so the gun floats disembodied and gets stretched into the corner because the viewmodel shares the world FOV instead of a narrower one. Materials are the harder failure: one flat blue-grey value across the entire body with zero edge wear, no metalness response picking up that bright sky, and no specular breakup along the barrel, while the muzzle flash is a ~40px orange blob sitting above the bore line that casts no light onto the weapon or ground and has no smoke or petal shape, and the ejected shell is a uniform flat-yellow capsule with no rim, primer, or tumble, floating well right of an ejection port that does not exist on the model.

panel.why: In A the optic has an actual glass pane, a knurled elevation turret with machined 1/2/3 detents and hex screws, edge-worn paint on the rail slots, and the muzzle flash visibly spills warm light onto the handguard while the ejected brass shows an extractor groove, primer ring and directional blur; in B the weapon is visibly faceted (the barrel's cylinder segments are countable), the metal is a flat matte blue-grey with no specular or environment response so it reads as painted clay, the muzzle flash is a small four-point flare sprite that contributes zero light to the barrel beside it, and the ejected case is a tack-sharp gold pill floating over a heavily motion-blurred ground.
panel.weaponCraft: Proportions are legible as a wood-furniture shotgun and the raked hip-fire cant across the lower frame is a defensible pose, but the model is low-poly with unsmoothed facets on the barrel and forend cap, the receiver is a featureless box with no rail, screw, port or panel line, the wood is a flat vertical-streak texture with no grain or sheen, the metal has essentially no specular or env reflection so both materials read as painted clay, and the supporting hand is a grey fingerless mitten that clips into the forend with no contact AO. The muzzle flash fails hardest: it is a small four-point lens-flare cross sitting half behind the barrel silhouette that puts no light at all onto the receiver, wood or hand inches away, so the gun stays exactly as dark as an unfired frame, and the ejected shell is a flat gold cylinder with a hollow dark endcap (no rim, extractor groove or primer) rendered perfectly crisp against a heavily motion-blurred background, which reads as a sticker pasted onto the image rather than a case in flight.

panel.why: A carries authored layers B has none of — graffiti and grime decals over plank-by-plank boardwalk variation, a gloved hand with actual fingers wrapped around a rail-detailed receiver under a red dot with a numbered magnifier dial, and an explosion whose sparks trail with velocity into secondary smoke with correct bloom falloff — while B's entire viewmodel is a fingerless grey capsule resting on a faceted blockout, with a muzzle flare that lights nothing and a ground smeared into radial streaks while the sky and buildings behind it stay razor sharp.
panel.weaponCraft: The gun is a blockout, not a model: a cylinder barrel clipped into a slab receiver with no bevels, no edge wear and stair-stepped jaggies on every diagonal, a fore-end whose wood texture jumps value hard at each face seam, a rear sight that is two rectangular teeth on a black tab, and a "hand" that is a smooth fingerless capsule floating on the handguard with zero contact shadow or AO — and it's framed so the stock, trigger, trigger guard and magazine simply cease to exist below the bottom edge, with the barrel axis pointing somewhere other than screen centre so it reads as parked in frame rather than aimed. The muzzle flash is a flat additive starburst that looks like a lens flare and, fatally, throws no light onto the barrel, the hand or the ground an inch away, and the ejected shell is a uniform gold tube with flat-cut ends — no rim, no extractor groove, no primer, no brass-to-hull split — hanging pin-sharp and motionless while the terrain beside it is blurred to mush, emerging from a receiver that has no ejection port cut into it at all.
